message.content:
There isn’t one definitive “best” jazz vocalist—different listeners value different styles—but here are a few names most people would agree have had enormous influence:

| Singer | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-----------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** (1930s‑1960s) | Known for her emotive phrasing and unique vocal timbre – classic recordings like *“Strange Fruit,”* *“God Bless the Child.”* |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** (1940s‑1990s) | Renowned as “the First Lady of Song”; celebrated scat technique and impeccable diction – albums such as *“Song Book” series.* |
| **Sarah Vaughan** (1950s‑2001) | Her rich contralto range earned her nicknames “Sassy” or “Little Bird.” She blended blues, swing, and bebop effortlessly. |
| **Nina Simone** (1950s‑2003) | Though she crossed into soul/R&B, her jazz roots were strong; powerful interpretations of standards and originals alike. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** (1980s‑present) | Modern voice blending traditional jazz with folk/rock influences; known for deep, resonant tone. |

These artists each brought something distinct to jazz vocals—from emotional depth to technical mastery—and continue to inspire new generations.
